clue.text: Play area foundation entirely covered by black stone

indicators.note: in an across answer, a part covered by another sits after it, so the covering letter comes first

parts.note: a foundation is a base
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
entirely means all of it
a diamond is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A playground built on a base set entirely beneath dark paving stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covered by' puts the black letter on top of the word for 'entirely', which in a row means in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The infield of a baseball ground, marked out as a square of bases, is the space where the game is played.

clue.text: Comparatively tough person delighting in violence

definitions.meaning: first meaning: more butch, the comparative of an adjective meaning macho
second meaning: a brutal killer who revels in slaughter

explanation.surface: A description of someone harder than the rest who enjoys bloodshed.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as butch plus the comparative ending -ER, a sense the solver rarely notices in a familiar word.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively a butcher is a savage, bloodthirsty murderer, and butch with -er gives the comparative adjective meaning more macho.

clue.text: Particular mounted circuits core to pricey electronic parts

indicators.note: in a down answer, something mounted climbs upward, so the letters read from bottom to top
to part something is to split it open, so other letters push into the gap

parts.note: circuits of a track are laps

indicators.note: the core of a word is its centre, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the word
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Expensive electronic components have their own specially mounted circuit boards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' is a verb: the middle of 'pricey' plus E split the word for circuits, and the whole is then written upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adjectives describing something singled out or out of the ordinary, as in a special or particular case.

clue.text: Grouse positioned around wood to mass over large fruit

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it on both sides

parts.note: to grouse or beef is to complain
something sat somewhere is positioned there
teak is a hardwood
taken as written
M is the symbol for mass in physics
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A gamebird is placed around timber in a pile on top of some big fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like the bird but is the verb to complain. The verb for 'positioned' wraps the wood, 'to' and the mass symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: This variety of tomato is the biggest commonly grown, so it is a specific example of a large fruit.

clue.text: One won't shift rioter fixed with glue, oddly ignored

indicators.note: something fixed has been rigged or rearranged, so its letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones

parts.note: the second and fourth letters survive

explanation.surface: A protester glued down to stop being moved on is someone who refuses to budge.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes climate protesters gluing themselves to roads; 'fixed' is the anagram signal, not the glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lingers idly and will not move on is said to loiter, so a person who won't shift is one.

clue.text: Brought to light, wooden boat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: excavated or unearthed, as in found something buried
second meaning: a canoe made by hollowing out a tree trunk

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is the two-word verb phrase; the second is the single noun for a hollowed log canoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Unearthing something reveals it, and a canoe carved from a single log carries the same name as the phrasal verb.

clue.text: I, perhaps, inspect alternative ways to enter workplace

indicators.note: an alternative version of these letters is a different arrangement of them

parts.note: all fifteen letters, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: A hesitant inspector considers other routes into a job.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder runs across the commas: the whole of 'I, perhaps, inspect' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Training schemes where newcomers learn a trade on the job are a common route into employment.

clue.text: Shock as king's admitted to lack of power

indicators.note: someone admitted is let inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a power outage is a blackout
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Scandal as a monarch is caught up in a power cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the king to his admission.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrage is a strong feeling of shock and anger, so either word names the reaction to something scandalous.

clue.text: Composed doctor? Not totally, following day

indicators.note: what is not total falls short of complete, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: DR is the standard abbreviation for doctor
coming after something is following it
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Was the doctor calm? Not entirely, the day after something happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' looks like calm, an adjective describing the doctor, but it is the past tense of writing something. The question mark splits the clue into a misleading exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: To draft a letter or speech is to write a first version of it, so drafted works as a past tense for composed.

clue.text: Swaying chime on The Beatles' Now and Then

indicators.note: in an across answer, something put on another is placed after it
now and then means at intervals, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters
a bell's chime is a ring

explanation.surface: A wavering bell sound on the Beatles' last single, Now and Then, released in 2023.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now and Then' is a real Beatles song title, which hides its role as the signal to take alternate letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To teeter is to wobble unsteadily, so something teetering is swaying back and forth on the point of falling.

clue.text: Cavity at back displaying Middle-Eastern fare

parts.note: a pit is a hole or cavity

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so letters read right to left

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hole in the back of the mouth shows something to do with Middle Eastern food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At back' reads as a location but is a tiny word turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat bread with a pocket is a staple of Greek and Middle Eastern cooking, so an example of that food.

clue.text: Has problems to put on hotel showers

indicators.note: in an across answer, a part put on another sits after it

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
something that ails has trouble

explanation.surface: A hotel guest complains that the showers are faulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Showers' looks like the bathroom fitting, but it is a verb: pours down.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail is to rain down in quantity, as blows or praise may, which is to shower someone.

clue.text: Joyous aunt with beer drunk receiving kiss

indicators.note: to receive is to take something in, so one piece holds another
a drunk is in a muddle, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A tipsy aunt full of beer is merry as she gets a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: X for a kiss comes from the crosses signed at the end of letters; it slips inside the jumbled aunt and beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant describes high-spirited, lively enthusiasm, close in sense to joyful and cheerful.

clue.text: No longer anxious priest: first woman accepted, in a way

indicators.note: one thing in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road

indicators.note: what is accepted is taken on board and added, so pieces are joined in sequence

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible
Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A cleric is reassured once the first female candidate is ordained, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' sounds like a hedge but means inside a road. ELI is the crossword's favourite priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling relief means the worry has gone, so someone relieved is free of their earlier anxiety.

clue.text: Tramp concerned about little shelters

indicators.note: to shelter something is to cover it, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
RE means concerning or about

explanation.surface: A vagrant worries about the small huts where he sleeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a noun for a vagrant but is the verb to walk heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk with heavy steps, and treading is likewise walking or stamping on something.

clue.text: Criminal behaviour having one in gang shot

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: a band is a group or gang
I is the Roman numeral one
a shot at something is a try

explanation.surface: Lawlessness in which a gang member was gunned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a gunshot but means an attempt; the numeral sits inside 'gang' plus 'shot' put together.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditry is robbery and lawless violence by armed outlaws, a form of criminal conduct.

clue.text: Endure moments cycling

indicators.note: going round in a cycle moves the last letter to the front

parts.note: a tick is a moment, as in just a tick

explanation.surface: Putting up with a few moments on a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The final S of TICKS comes round to the front. 'Just a tick' is British for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick something out, or simply stick it, is to tolerate or bear it, a sense common in British usage.

clue.text: One intolerant to 15 bananas, if fresh

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone allergic to fresh bananas, as though talking of food intolerance.
explanation.walkthrough: 15 is BANDITRY, so the definition is someone who won't tolerate outlaws; 'bananas' looks like food beside 'intolerant' and 'fresh'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Westerns the lawman who hunts outlaws is the county's chief peace officer, so he cannot abide robbery.

clue.text: Person with specialist knowledge announced drink that's popular?

indicators.note: something announced is spoken, so we hear rather than read it

parts.note: popular is IN and the drink is CIDER, so a fashionable drink is in cider

explanation.surface: An expert declares which drink is fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: IN is the crossword's usual word for popular; spoken together with the apple drink it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider is someone within an organisation who has privileged inside information unavailable to the public.

clue.text: Vessel of gold church obscured with cross

indicators.note: something obscured is hidden from view, covered by what surrounds it

parts.note: to span a river is to cross it
AU is the chemical symbol for gold
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A golden church chalice partly hidden by a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'church' suggest a chalice, and 'cross' a crucifix; here cross is a verb, to bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucepan is a cooking pot with a handle, and a vessel is any container for liquids.

clue.text: Bird enclosure collapse, needing to make top good

indicators.note: making the top something else swaps the first letter for a new one

parts.note: a pen is an animal enclosure
to collapse is to fall to ruin
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: An aviary falls down and its roof must be repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the top is the first letter, so RUIN's R gives way to G.
explanation.definitionFit: A penguin is a flightless seabird of the Southern Hemisphere, so a specific example of a bird.

clue.text: Issue tenders working here?

parts.note: surface reading: a place where bids for a contract are issued, like a procurement office
setter's reading: issue is offspring, so those who tend children work at this place

explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue tenders' reads as putting out contract bids; 'issue' means children and the tenders are the people looking after them.
explanation.definitionFit: A day-care centre for small children is staffed by carers who look after the young ones.

clue.text: City home that's stretched dough

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
a lair is an animal's home

explanation.surface: Living in the City is expensive enough to stretch one's money, dough being slang for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcode begins EC.
explanation.definitionFit: This pastry is choux paste piped into a long finger shape, so it is literally elongated pastry.

clue.text: Comfortably settled hens conceded boxes

indicators.note: something that boxes another encloses it, so the letters sit inside the words

parts.note: runs from the second letter of the first word to near the end of the second

explanation.surface: Hens settled in their nesting boxes after giving up a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxes' sounds like the hens' nesting boxes but is a verb signalling that the answer is contained.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ensconced is to be snugly established in a safe, comfortable spot.

clue.text: Fly high having installed new navigation system

indicators.note: something installed is fitted inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to soar is to fly high
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An aircraft takes off after a new navigation system is fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly high' looks like the aircraft's action in the story, but it supplies the outer word that receives the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonar uses sound echoes to locate objects underwater, and ships and submarines use it to find their way.

clue.text: Sign admiral regularly noted is part of code

indicators.note: noting at regular intervals means only every other letter is recorded

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: An admiral's signal was recorded as part of a secret code.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters come from 'Sign admiral' together, so the selection crosses the word break.
explanation.definitionFit: In the NATO phonetic alphabet used for radio spelling, the letter I is represented by this country's name.

clue.text: Quality woolly attire covering on the other hand

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap round it, so one piece holds another
something woolly is fuzzy and confused, so the letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written
but introduces a contrast, like on the other hand

explanation.surface: Good-quality knitwear covering, though possibly not, on the other hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woolly' looks like a description of knitted clothing but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An attribute is a characteristic or property that something has, which is one sense of quality.

clue.text: Pro solver's agreed on terms of personal methodology being top secret

parts.note: pro means in favour of
the solver is addressed as you, so solver's is you are
yes signals agreement
taken as written

indicators.note: a term is an end point, so only each word's final letter is taken

parts.note: the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: An expert puzzler agrees to explain their technique only if it stays confidential.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'solver' is you, so 'solver's' is the contraction you're. The James Bond film title is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is stamped on classified documents meant for one reader alone, which is a highly confidential marking.
